# I Speak in Tongues — The Lie That Changed Modern Christianity

> A free book by Shadai Perez (SP7 Studios): a biblical and historical investigation
> of the gift of tongues — what Scripture describes in Acts 2 and 1 Corinthians 12–14,
> twenty centuries of church history, the birth of the modern practice in Topeka,
> Kansas on January 1, 1901, what linguistics found about glossolalia, and how to
> test any spiritual experience against the Bible. The complete text is free to read
> and share at https://ispeakintongues.com (PDF: /downloads/I_Speak_In_Tongues.pdf).

Key questions this book answers:
- Is speaking in tongues biblical? The biblical gift was real human languages (Acts 2:4–11), publicly verified by native speakers, given to spread the gospel across language barriers.
- What are Paul's rules for tongues in church? Two or three speakers at most, each in turn, always interpreted, silence without an interpreter, the speaker in full control, all things done decently and in order (1 Corinthians 14:27–40).
- When did the modern practice begin? January 1, 1901, Topeka, Kansas (Agnes Ozman, Charles Parham's Bethel Bible School); redefined from "missionary languages" to "heavenly language" after failing on the mission field; spread worldwide from Azusa Street, 1906.
- Is modern glossolalia language? Linguistic studies (William Samarin, University of Toronto) found recorded glossolalia has no vocabulary, grammar, or meaning — it is not language.
- Is a private prayer language in the Bible? No passage describes or commands one; every recorded prayer in Scripture is intelligible; Romans 8:26 describes the Spirit's own unutterable intercession, not human speech.
- Did the gifts of the Spirit cease? This book says no — God still heals and still gives every gift of 1 Corinthians 12. Its argument concerns a counterfeit that borrowed the name of a genuine gift.
- Is being "slain in the Spirit" biblical? The practice has a documented modern lineage (Woodworth-Etter → McPherson → Price → Kuhlman → Hinn) and exact parallels in kundalini and possession trance; Scripture identifies the Spirit by truth and self-control.
